organization.description: Stratum Graphene Technologies manufactures large-area monolayer graphene via roll-to-roll chemical vapor deposition (CVD)—sheet and interlayer products only; the company does not pursue carbon nanotube (CNT) or carbon nanoparticle structural additives, consistent with DARPA-SN-26-62 scope. Stratum performs scalable transfer and lamination into aerospace-qualified epoxy systems and operates a mechanical testing laboratory focused on composite fatigue, interlaminar shear, and compression-after-impact. Claims to government customers are anchored to measured structural coupons, joint lap-shear/ILSS surrogates, and factory throughput and yield observations—not modeling-only narratives or uncorroborated theoretical performance.

technical_poc.name: Dr. Samuel Okonkwo
technical_poc.title: Chief Technology Officer
technical_poc.background_summary: Materials scientist with 16 years in aerospace composites manufacturing and qualification (AS9100 environments). Led teams qualifying carbon/epoxy prepreg structures for UAV primary structures and introduced monolayer-graphene interleaf concepts with statistically powered fatigue datasets (stress-life curves, environmental conditioning per ASTM)—always tied to physical specimens, not stand-alone simulation. For DARPA-SN-26-62, responses emphasize coupon-level substantiation, line-rate and yield metrics from manufacturing, and explicit avoidance of CNT-based approaches and modeling-only structural assertions.

focus_areas: Roll-to-roll monolayer graphene synthesis and defect mapping (no CNT / nanoparticle structural fillers)
Transfer & lamination into aerospace epoxy systems (controlled void content)
Structural composites testing: tension/compression, ILSS, CAI, fatigue—coupon and sub-element evidence first
Hybrid laminates: monolayer graphene interlayers vs baseline carbon fiber/epoxy under matched manufacturing controls
Manufacturing throughput, yield, and floor observation as primary scale-up evidence
Empirical cost modeling ($/lb) grounded in measured scrap, cycle time, and labor—not FEA-derived structural claims
research_profile.research_description: Stratum pairs scalable monolayer graphene sheet supply with statistically framed structural validation using physical coupons and elements. Load-bearing claims are demonstrated through identical-cure comparisons of baseline UD carbon/epoxy versus graphene-interleaved stacks (lap-shear, ILSS, static, fatigue, conditioning per ASTM). Through-thickness behavior is explored via Mode I/II fracture surrogates when data exists—not as modeling-only predictions. Scale-up and barrier discussions cite line rates, rework, web breaks, and QC binning from the factory floor. Stratum does not position carbon nanotubes or nanoparticle additives as part of its structural roadmap for this RFI.
research_profile.prior_experience: Delivered pilot-line graphene interlayers for a regional UAV OEM demonstrator wing spar cap (non-flight article); joint testing campaign with a Tier 1 aerostructures supplier comparing fatigue crack growth trends vs baseline laminate under matched spectrum loading.

project_goals.primary_objective: Provide DARPA/TTO with empirical, manufacturing-grounded insight into monolayer graphene sheet scalability, joining strategies, structural substantiation from coupons and elements, and realistic weight/cost trades for aerospace load-bearing structures. The response aligns with RFI exclusions: no carbon nanotube or nanoparticle structural approaches, no modeling-only structural claims, and no non–load-bearing sensor angles unless explicitly tied to structural substantiation. Assertions are tied to measured coupons, joint tests, and factory throughput and yield—not uncorroborated theory.

technical_goals.title: Document largest manufacturable graphene sheet dimensions & grading methodology
technical_goals.description: Report roll-width/continuous length limits for monolayer graphene sheets suitable for structural lamination, including thickness uniformity definitions and defect thresholds tied to mechanical bins.
technical_goals.success_metric: Clear dimensional envelope + QC correlation to lap-shear / ILSS surrogate metrics.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: White paper Section + summary tables (within 5-page constraint).

technical_goals.title: Outline scalable joining pathways for larger aerostructure blanks
technical_goals.description: Describe overlap/scarf strategies for graphene-bearing prepreg stacks; discuss process sensitivities (voids, resin starvation) and tested lap-shear performance distributions.
technical_goals.success_metric: Empirical lap-shear datasets for at least two joining configurations under controlled cure.

technical_goals.title: Quantify barriers to production-scale sheets at aerospace quality
technical_goals.description: Enumerate throughput limits, yield loss drivers, environmental controls, and capital barriers—mapped to realistic ramp timelines.
technical_goals.success_metric: Traceable barrier list grounded in factory observations.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: Bullet narrative aligned to RFI requested information items.

technical_goals.title: Structural substantiation: static & fatigue evidence
technical_goals.description: Present coupon/element-level results for in-plane tension/compression, ILSS, and fatigue (R-ratio stated) vs baseline carbon/epoxy control panels matched on fiber areal weight.
technical_goals.success_metric: Statistically meaningful sample sizes (n≥5 per configuration per environment unless noted).

technical_goals.title: Weight reduction & cost estimates
technical_goals.description: Provide conservative weight reduction estimate for equal strength/stiffness targets derived from or bounded by coupon-derived allowables and sub-element tests—not FEA-only stacks. Provide $/lb manufacturing cost basis from observed scrap, cure cycle time, labor, and capital amortization on the actual line.
technical_goals.success_metric: Assumptions table that cites specimen IDs / test standards where strength/stiffness equivalency is claimed; cost sensitivity to yield and fiber price using floor data.
technical_goals.deliverable_aligned: Summary tables within RFI page limits; figures from physical tests where applicable.

expected_outcomes.deliverable: RFI white paper (≤5 pages) addressing all six technical areas with figures
expected_outcomes.description: Structured per DARPA-SN-62 submission format; proprietary details marked per instructions.
expected_outcomes.transition_plan: If DARPA issues a follow-on program, Stratum can expand datasets under contract—RFI does not bind either party.

project_goals.fundamental_research_justification: RFI response emphasizes controlled experiments, coupon-level structural evidence, and manufacturing economics—not unrestricted publication and not modeling-only structural assertions.
project_goals.revolutionary_vs_evolutionary: Positions graphene interlayers as a potential evolutionary-but-material weight/stiffness lever when manufacturing-controlled—not a replacement for primary fiber architecture without substantiation.
project_goals.competitive_landscape: Multiple vendors claim large-area graphene; Stratum differentiates with traceable coupon and element datasets, line-rate and yield transparency, and explicit alignment with RFI boundaries (no CNTs/particles; no modeling-only pitches).
project_goals.transition_and_commercialization: Primary transition path is insertion as qualified interlayer/adhesive additive into existing carbon/epoxy supply chains for UAV and regional jet tier suppliers.

compliance_and_constraints.special_considerations: DARPA-SN-26-62 excludes carbon nanotube material or particles in these applications and discourages modeling-only and uncorroborated theoretical responses. Stratum's RFI narrative is limited to monolayer graphene sheet and interlayer approaches, grounded in measured structural coupons and elements, joint characterization data, and manufacturing throughput and yield observations. Simulation or FEA, if mentioned at all, is ancillary to interpretation of physical data—not a substitute for substantiation.
